title: [BugFix][Core] Promote parked skipped_waiting requests under saturation
body_opening:
## Purpose

Fix the promotion-starvation mechanism analyzed in #53130.

Requests parked in `skipped_waiting` (`WAITING_FOR_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_GRAMMAR` / `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` / `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ`) are only promoted while the waiting loop of `schedule()` traverses them, and that loop stops on the token-budget and `max_num_seqs` capacity checks. On steps where running requests consume the entire token budget (e.g. long chunked prefills) or occupy every request slot, the loop never reaches the parked requests, so:

- a parked request whose grammar has finished compiling is never promoted, and
- a parked request whose grammar compile **failed** is never detected and never terminated.

title: [TurboQuant] Share decode scratch workspace across layers
body_opening:
## Summary

TurboQuant currently registers temporary decode scratch buffers per attention
layer. Those buffers scale with the number of TurboQuant layers and
`max_num_seqs`, which can consume tens of GiB of non-KV memory on large models.

This PR moves TurboQuant decode scratch allocation to the v1 workspace manager
so the scratch tensors are shared across layers. It also reserves the maximum
TurboQuant workspace from the TurboQuant metadata-builder initialization path,
before CUDA graph capture locks the workspace.

This PR is scoped to TurboQuant decode scratch memory usage and locked-workspace
growth. It does not claim to fix unrelated TurboQuant speculative-decoding
correctness issues.

- Has `add_bos_token: false` in its tokenizer configuration
- Expects prompts to be formatted with specific role markers (e.g., `<|start_of_role|>user<|end_of_role|>...`)

body_opening:
## Motivation
